title: Expansion protocol public hardening
description: Objective: publish and independently compose the complete pure Expansion admission protocol after every sibling lands, then run the parent-level regression/adversarial gate. Hard dependencies: tasks task-7f089e11daea44e9a483197ff139d725, task-fcad40b6d26243439cd19fd3e49c924d, task-93b0314e09f248118e21f92699989468, task-2561a780fdd149439c9858c9c7b459e8, and task-b863bae80fab426db7b6204f9d713c42 must be DONE. Certified capabilities: runner-safe expansion hold/request, hold-bound PlanningRun submission, all-or-none scheduler admission/preparation, and exact manual approval binding shipped by those tasks. Deliverable: curated @moe/core/@moe/scheduler root surfaces and one production-surface integration/mutation suite; real durable consumer remains task-9634ed3b72014fe781591c7df9674da2. NOT in scope: daemon persistence, child activation, UI, or adding authority. Owned paths: packages/core/src/index.ts, packages/core/src/index-surface.test.ts, packages/scheduler/src/index.ts, packages/scheduler/src/index-surface.test.ts, tests/integration/expansion-protocol.test.ts. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/core typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/core test && pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test && pnpm exec vitest run tests/integration/expansion-protocol.test.ts.
definitionOfDone: The curated core and scheduler root namespaces export the complete expansion value/type closure and all prerequisite admission symbols required by the protocol; exact namespace tests and plain-Node bare-package probes pass with no deep imports.

The integration test drives only production root surfaces through valid request/hold, EXPANSION submission, evidence/admission/preparation, and manual approval, byte-compares the exact bound identities, and asserts that no pure stage exposes child/run/lease/effect/slot/allocation activation/dispatch authority.

A generated refusal/race matrix covers every declared expansion code and refusing layer, asserts nonzero cases, exact delegated layer ownership, changed-delta reapproval, all-or-none outputs, UNKNOWN denial, and boundary 3/6/9 against production—not helper—surfaces.

An adversarial whole-sibling review mutates/bypasses hold, quality, scope, oracle, input, dependency, budget, resource, fairness capacity, preparation, and approval guards one at a time and proves the focused/integration suite turns red before restoring production bytes.

The exact foreground verification command exits 0 with every production file below 400 lines; foreign baseline failures are path-attributed, no docs/debug/generated evidence remain, and task-9634ed3b72014fe781591c7df9674da2 is recorded as the durable consumer.
taskRails: This task certifies only the pure protocol shipped by the five named tasks; durable atomic child authority is certified later by daemon composition.
Do not reimplement authority or acceptance predicates inside the integration test.
Root publication must be curated and exact; no wildcard collision or deep-import workaround.

implementationPlan.note:
packages/core/src/index-surface.test.ts created (did not exist; owned path). Core legs green: typecheck exit 0; test exit 0, 27 files / 549 tests (baseline 26 / 471).

ARITHMETIC ON THE GROWTH, because "+78 tests" is exactly the kind of number that hides a miscount: 69 it.each namespace cases + 9 hand-written its = 78, and 471 + 78 = 549. If the count pin had been raised without the list entries the it.each would have generated 69 and the name-set equality would have failed instead.

WHAT IT PINS
- EXPECTED_EXPORTS: 69 hand-transcribed [name, kind] pairs, kinds array/function/record/string. Hand-transcribed, never derived from the namespace under test, so a removal AND an unreviewed addition both go red. `toBe(69)` for the count, plus `Object.keys(core).filter(k => k !== "default").sort()` equality against the list, plus a per-name kind case.
- The undefined check runs FIRST inside each case and is phrased as `expect("NAME=defined")`, not `expect(value).toBeDefined()`. An import cycle yields a TDZ-undefined binding that imports cleanly, satisfies `typeof value === "undefined"` and only fails at first use; making the name part of the compared string means the failure message says which export died rather than "expected undefined to be defined".

WHAT IT PROVES ABOUT TYPES, and why it is here rather than in the integration suite. tests/integration/** is typechecked by no gate, so a type annotation there is transpiled away and proves nothing. All 25 published core expansion types are annotated in THIS file, on values that came through the bare `@moe/core` specifier, where `pnpm --filter @moe/core typecheck` sees them. This is not theoretical: the first run failed with `src/index-surface.test.ts(204,17): error TS2339: Property 'outcome' does not exist on type 'ExpansionPolicyFacts'` — I had assumed the field name. The annotations are load-bearing enough to have already caught one wrong assumption of mine, which is the best evidence they are not decorative.

FIXTURES ARE TYPED, NOT CAST. My first draft reached the prepared value through `as unknown as ExpansionPreparationInput`, which asserts a shape instead of checking it — a published type that drifted from what prepareExpansion accepts would have sailed through. Rewritten so preparationInput() RETURNS ExpansionPreparationInput, policyInput() returns PolicyEvaluationInput, humanApproval() returns ApprovalDecisionRecord and approvalRequest() returns ExpansionApprovalRequest, all as plain typed literals with no casts anywhere. tsc now checks every fixture field against the published contract.

FIVE BEHAVIOURAL TESTS, each pinning code AND component AND layer rather than "it refused": one preparation accepted (hex64 identity, policy decision REQUIRE_HUMAN_APPROVAL from the R2 human-only tier, all three reservation states, the sources echo); one preparation refused with EXPANSION_PREPARATION_GRAPH_NOT_SUPERSEDABLE / GRAPH_REVISION / LIFECYCLE — note the component is a DELEGATED surface, not this module, so a re-coded refusal would fail here; one manual approval accepted with the binding's preparationIdentity byte-compared to the preparation it came from; one non-human approval refused with EXPANSION_APPROVAL_RECORD_INVALID / INPUT; and all six core expansion vocabularies asserted frozen.

THE PLAIN-NODE PROBE (DoD 1). execFileAsync(process.execPath, ["--experimental-strip-types", "--input-type=module", "-e", source], { cwd: PACKAGE_ROOT, timeout }), mechanism copied from packages/control-room-client/src/control-room-client-runtime-entrypoint.test.ts including the kill timeout, so a hung child is reaped rather than outliving the run. cwd at the package root makes the bare `@moe/core` specifier resolve through this package's own exports map by Node's self-reference rule — the resolution @moe/scheduler and @moe/daemon actually get.
It asserts RUNTIME VALUES, which is the whole point: strip-types erases every `export type`, so a closure published only as types satisfies tsc and arrives here with nothing importable. namedExportCount 69, undefinedBindingCount 0, typeof on prepareExpansion / approveExpansionManually / reduceExpansionPlanningHold / reducePlanningRun, and the two vocabularies compared by LITERAL ARRAY EQUALITY rather than by length — a frozen array that lost a member keeps its type and its arity check.

NEGATIVE CONTROL, and the reason the probe above is not vacuous: importing ./src/index-surface.test.js must fail with the literal ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND. It proves both that test-tier code stayed off the runtime surface and that a broken probe would report FAILED rather than quietly reporting IMPORTED for a package that never loaded. Pinning the literal code rather than "it threw" is what makes that second half real.

implementationPlan.description:
Create tests/integration/expansion-protocol.test.ts — DoD 2, the acceptance journey. The root vitest config already includes `tests/**/*.test.ts`, so it will be collected; confirm the Test Files count grows.

Drive ONLY PRODUCTION ROOT SURFACES — `@moe/core` and `@moe/scheduler` bare specifiers, no deep imports, no relative reach into src/ (taskRail 3). If the journey needs a symbol the roots do not export, that is a step-2/3 publication gap, not a licence to deep-import.

The journey in order: valid request/hold -> EXPANSION submission -> evidence/admission/preparation -> manual approval. BYTE-COMPARE the exact bound identities at each stage rather than checking shapes — the identity binding is the protocol's whole guarantee, so assert exact equality and, for a perturbed input, exact inequality.

DoD 2's zero-authority clause is a distinct assertion: prove NO pure stage exposes child, run, lease, effect, slot, allocation-activation or dispatch authority. Assert the ABSENCE positively over each stage's output rather than trusting the shape — an accepted result carrying a lease reference would satisfy every happy-path check.

taskRail 2: do NOT reimplement acceptance predicates in the test. Call the production validators; a test that re-derives "is this admissible" is asserting against itself.

THE ONE REAL DEVIATION FROM THE PLAN, and it is a correction to the plan rather than a shortcut. The step says to drive the journey through bare `@moe/core` / `@moe/scheduler` specifiers. THAT IS UNSATISFIABLE FROM tests/. pnpm links workspace packages into each CONSUMING package's node_modules, never into the repo root, and tests/ belongs to no package, so the first run died with "Cannot find package '@moe/core' imported from D:/projexts/moe-next/tests/integration/expansion-protocol.test.ts" — a failure every package in this workspace shares, including ones whose bridges have been correct for months.
I did NOT resolve it by adding root devDependencies: that would mutate the root manifest and the shared pnpm-lock, and require a global `pnpm install` in a worktree other agents are building in.
Instead I followed the convention every existing suite under tests/integration/ already uses — relative paths — restricted to the two package ROOT ENTRIES, `../../packages/{core,scheduler}/src/index.js`, exactly the modules the exports maps publish. The curation property taskRail 3 protects is fully preserved: a symbol the barrels do not export is unreachable here for the same reason it is unreachable for a real consumer.
And it is enforced mechanically rather than promised. Two guard tests read this file's own source and assert (a) every import specifier is one of stdlib/vitest/the two root entries and (b) every workspace specifier equals the two root entries exactly. That a REAL consumer resolves those roots through the exports map is proven separately and more strongly by the bare-specifier probes in packages/core/src/index-surface.test.ts and the bare `@moe/scheduler` imports in the scheduler surface test.

MY OWN GUARD CAUGHT ME WRITING A PROSE-MATCHING BOUNDARY CHECK. The first version of guard (b) scanned for any quoted `@moe/...` anywhere in the file and went red on the header comment that EXPLAINS why bare specifiers do not work. Rewritten to anchor on the import/export STATEMENT, so a path named in a comment can neither pass nor fail it — and a new deep import cannot hide behind one either.

THE JOURNEY, in order, every stage driven by a production function: hold (reduceExpansionPlanningHold) -> EXPANSION draft and sealed proposal (reducePlanningRun) -> evidence and admission (deriveExpansionEvidence, admitExpansion) -> core preparation and manual approval (prepareExpansion, approveExpansionManually).

IDENTITIES ARE BYTE-COMPARED, NOT SHAPE-CHECKED. The hold's creationReceipt.command equals the caller's command object exactly; the sealed proposal's proposalHash equals the run's submissionHash; the admission's bound childKeys/sourceDigests/childWidth equal the DERIVED evidence's, never the receipt's own claims; the core preparation's admitted.evidenceDigest and admitted.proposalId equal the scheduler's; the approval binding's preparationIdentity equals the preparation identity. Determinism is pinned by running the whole journey twice and comparing all three identities.
The inverse is pinned too: 9 scheduler perturbations and 5 core perturbations, each changing ONE byte, each asserted to move its identity. The scheduler set additionally asserts all 10 identities are DISTINCT — "different from base" would pass if every perturbation collapsed onto one shared wrong value. Each perturbation asserts ACCEPTANCE first, because a perturbation that merely got refused would also "not equal" the base and would prove nothing. Both sweeps pin their case count so a sweep that generated zero cases cannot pass while testing nothing.

CHANGED-DELTA REAPPROVAL is a real refusal, not a shape check: the original claim is presented against a preparation whose deadlineEpochMs moved, and the result is pinned to EXPANSION_APPROVAL_PREPARATION_MISMATCH and asserted to be a member of the published EXPANSION_APPROVAL_CODES.

ZERO AUTHORITY (DoD 2) IS ASSERTED POSITIVELY, AND A BLANKET BAN WOULD HAVE BEEN WRONG. The hold legitimately carries leaseRef, providerSlotRef and terminalEffectRefs — that is RELEASE EVIDENCE, proof authority was given UP, the opposite of minting it. A `/run|lease|effect|slot/` key ban would have failed on correct code and taught me to weaken it. So each stage's authority-shaped key set is pinned by an EXACT hand-written list with every entry justified inline (hold: 9 keys, incl. `release` itself, which matches only because the word contains "lease"; sealed run: 6; scheduler admission: exactly ["effectIntentRefs"], an intent recorded against a reservation that was never activated; core preparation and approval binding: EMPTY). A newly minted authority key anywhere fails the set equality. The semantic half is asserted beside it: attemptState/leaseState/providerSlotState are

implementationPlan.description:
DoD 3 — the generated refusal/race matrix, driven against PRODUCTION surfaces, never helpers. Cover every declared expansion code and its refusing layer, and assert a NON-ZERO case count plus that each declared case was actually generated — a sweep that silently produces zero cases passes while testing nothing.

Six properties the matrix must pin, each easy to assert weakly:
  - EXACT DELEGATED LAYER OWNERSHIP: where a refusal originates in a composed surface, the delegated code and layer pass through VERBATIM. Re-coding a delegated refusal loses which layer refused, which is the vacuous-assertion defect the global rail names.
  - CHANGED-DELTA REAPPROVAL: perturb any bound byte and assert re-approval is required, field by field.
  - ALL-OR-NONE outputs: a refusal leaves no partial reservation, preparation or approval behind — assert the absence of the artefacts, not just the returned refusal.
  - UNKNOWN DENIAL: an UNKNOWN fact never upgrades to a positive.
  - BOUNDARY 3/6/9: at the limit passes, one over refuses. Compose EXPANSION_LIMITS from packages/scheduler/src/admission/admission-records.ts:22 rather than writing the literals — a local copy forks the limit authority.
  - RACES: approve against release/invalidate/expiry/reprepare.
implementationPlan.note:
DoD 3 refusal/race matrix landed in tests/integration/expansion-protocol.test.ts. `pnpm exec vitest run tests/integration/expansion-protocol.test.ts` exits 0, 110 tests (34 before this step).

COVERAGE IS EXACT AGAINST THE PRODUCTION VOCABULARIES, and guarded against the way that check normally rots. Each table's produced code set is compared by SET EQUALITY to the published frozen array — evidence 11, admission-local 3, preparation 9, approval 20. That alone would be self-policing: delete a code from production AND from the table and both sides shrink together, leaving the suite green and one guard silently retired. So every vocabulary's LENGTH is additionally pinned to a hand-written literal (11 / 3 / 9 / 20), and the evidence table also compares its case NAMES to a hand-written list. A shrunken table now fails on the count, and a shrunken vocabulary fails on the length.
Counts: 11 evidence + 3 admission-local + 5 delegated origins + 9 preparation + 21 approval cases (20 distinct codes; BUDGET_MISMATCH is reached twice, by a moved binding byte and by the release race, and both are worth keeping). Every case pins CODE and LAYER, and every core case pins COMPONENT too.

DELEGATED LAYER OWNERSHIP IS PROVED BY COMPARISON, NOT BY TRANSCRIPTION. For all 11 evidence codes the matrix calls deriveExpansionEvidence DIRECTLY, then calls admitExpansion with the same receipt, and asserts the composed issue's code and layer equal the direct one's, with origin EVIDENCE. Pinning literals on both sides would not notice the two drifting together; comparing the composed refusal to the surface's own answer is what makes "verbatim" mean something. The other five composed origins — GRAPH, FAIRNESS, BUDGET, RESOURCE, LINEAGE — each get a case keeping their landed codes (ADMISSION_INPUT_MALFORMED, FAIRNESS_CONTRACT_UNDECLARED_RESOURCE, BUDGET_RESERVATION_STALE_VERSION, AUTHORITY_MALFORMED_INPUT, ADMISSION_EXPANSION_DEPTH_EXCEEDED), and a guard asserts the six declared origins are all exercised.

THE 3/6/9 BOUNDARY IS READ OUT OF PRODUCTION — and this is where the plan was wrong and I did not paper over it. Step 6 says to compose EXPANSION_LIMITS from admission-records.ts:22 rather than writing literals. That constant is NOT exported (measured in step 1), and its only escape is an AdmissionExpansionRecord that the accessor expansion-admission.ts actually calls discards. So it cannot be composed without adding an `export` to a file this task does not own.
The matrix instead DISCOVERS each boundary: it walks the dimension upward through admitExpansion until the named ADMISSION_EXPANSION_*_EXCEEDED code appears, and returns { lastAdmitted, firstRefused }, asserted to be {3,4} / {6,7} / {9,10}. Production decides where the boundary is, so nothing is forked; "at the limit passes, one over refuses" holds by construction rather than by two hand-written fixtures; and a limit change in production moves the discovery and reddens the pin. The walk THROWS on any refusal that is not the named limit code, so an unrelated failure can never be mistaken for a boundary — without that, a fixture that broke for some other reason would report a plausible wrong limit.

ALL-OR-NONE IS MEASURED, NOT READ OFF A FLAG. The late-failure case (budget reserved, then resources unavailable) asserts the refusal carries no preparation, identity, reservation or rows — each by name, so the failure message says WHICH artefact leaked — and then compares unwind.restoredMeters to the untouched caller view's meters. budgetReservationCancelled alone is satisfied by an implementation that strands the units in RESERVED, which is exactly why the meters are the assertion. The early-refusal case asserts the unwind is EMPTY: nothing was reserved before the parse, so nothing can have been given back. On the approval side every one of the 21 cases additionally asserts no binding was returned and that the caller's request bytes are unchanged.

UNKNOWN NEVER UPGRADES. An unclassifiable materialization yields disposition UNKNOWN from deriveExpansionEvidence AND from admitExpansion — pinned on both, because collapsing UNKNOWN into REFUSED is how a missing fact starts reading as a refuted one — with missingInput naming the exact path childScopes[0].inputs[0].materialization. A second case proves an UNKNOWN completion never becomes an admitted preparation.

RACES: eight post-preparation races, asserted as an ORDERED CODE LIST rather than a count, so a race that silently changed which code it produces fails instead of still counting as one of N. Budget released, resources released, approval invalidated, deadline expired, preparation gone stale, claim naming a re-prepared identity, supersession re-derived to a different authority, stored policy no longer yielding the bound decision.

THE HAPPY CONTROL IS ASSERTED FIRST: the unperturbed approval request is APPROVED before any case runs, so every refusal below is caused by its own perturbation and not by a fixture that was broken all alon

QA FULL EVIDENCE — qa-f3560083. APPROVED, all 5 DoD. Commit a069364, 8 files, 2086 insertions. Tree clean after my drills.

=== ALL FIVE GATE LEGS RE-RUN ===
core typecheck 0; core test 0 (27 files / 549); scheduler typecheck 0; scheduler test 0 (42 / 1137); `pnpm exec vitest run tests/integration/expansion-protocol.test.ts` 0 (1 / 113). Reproduces task.verification exactly.

=== THE BRIDGE-ORDERING CONSTRAINT HELD ===
I filed this constraint after task-b863bae8 and it was the thing I most expected to catch someone: exports from packages/core/src/index.ts and both `.js` bridges must land in the SAME commit, because export-without-bridges reddens runtime-entrypoint.test.ts with `missing` and bridges-without-export reddens it with `unexpected`, and there is no green intermediate state. Both bridges are in a069364 alongside the 34-line index.ts addition, and the core suite including that guard is green. Handled correctly.

=== THREE FILES OUTSIDE THE DECLARED OWNED PATHS, ALL LEGITIMATE ===
The two bridges are forced by the entrypoint guard — the case above, and the task that deferred them named this task as the one to add them.
supersession-engine.test.ts I did not take on trust; I tested it. Reverted that ONE file to its pre-task version and ran it alone: `AssertionError: expected 69 to be 61`. So publishing 8 new core root values necessarily broke that count guard — a red this diff caused, which per the rails is never disclosable and must be fixed. Fixing it was mandatory, not scope creep.

AND THE FIX IS THE RIGHT SHAPE, which matters more than that it was forced. A bare count 61 -> 69 would be satisfiable by any 8 symbols, and a RENAME would keep the count at 69 forever. It is backed by a hand-transcribed EXPECTED_EXPORTS list in the new index-surface.test.ts with `toBe(69)` AND a set-equality against the real root keys, so a rename fails the name list while the count still passes. The inline comment on the count says exactly this. Two guards that fail on different mutations, not one guard twice.

=== DoD 1 — POSITIVE AND NEGATIVE, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES IT A PROBE ===
`import * as core from "@moe/core"` (genuinely bare), a plain-Node `--experimental-strip-types` spawn probe, and at :376 a NEGATIVE CONTROL asserting `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` for an unbridged module. A publication probe without the negative half cannot distinguish "resolves" from "the harness never ran". No wildcard exports anywhere in the diff (`export *` absent), so rail 3's curation holds.

=== DoD 3 — GUARDED AGAINST THE WAY THIS CHECK NORMALLY ROTS ===
11 evidence + 3 admission + 9 preparation + 20 approval codes, set-compared to the published frozen arrays AND each length pinned to a hand-written literal. That pairing is the point: set equality alone is self-policing, because deleting a code from production and from the table shrinks both sides green. Now a shrunken table fails on count and a shrunken vocabulary fails on length.
Delegated ownership is proven by COMPARISON, not transcription: for all 11 evidence codes the matrix calls deriveExpansionEvidence directly, then admitExpansion, and asserts the composed code and layer equal the direct answer. Pinning literals on both sides would not notice the two drifting together.
The 3/6/9 boundary is DISCOVERED by walking production upward until the named code appears, asserted as {3,4}/{6,7}/{9,10}, with the walk THROWING on any refusal that is not the named limit code — so an unrelated failure can never be misread as a boundary. Better than the two hand-written fixtures the plan asked for, and the plan's suggested composition was genuinely unavailable (EXPANSION_LIMITS is unexported) — correctly reported rather than papered over with an unowned `export`.

=== DoD 4 — 15 MUTATIONS, 10 OF THE NAMED 11 RED, AND I REPRODUCED ONE ===
I drilled the scope guard independently (expansion-evidence.ts:126, `claimed.has(key)` -> `false`, with a no-op-mutation abort so a hash-identical edit could not read as a surviving guard). Result: 5 failed / 1245 passed, and the five span BOTH a sibling test ("refuses overlapping child scopes") AND two of this task's new cases ("refuses 'overlapping child scopes' with 'EXPANSION_SCOPE_OVERLAP' from 'SCOPE'" and "passes ... through admitExpansion VERBATIM, code and layer alike"). That is the evidence the matrix is load-bearing rather than restating coverage that already existed. Restored byte-exact, tree clean.

THE SURVIVOR — I verified the unreachability claim rather than accepting the production comment, because "defensive branch" is exactly what an unasserted guard also looks like. expansion-admission.ts:207 calls `rotateOnce(request.rotation)`; :208 returns early on failure; :214 calls `capacitySnapshot(request.rotation)` with the SAME input. So the branch at :152 is reachable only if validateResourceCapacity refuses a record rotateOnce already accepted — i.e. only if the two validators disagree, which is what the doc comment claims and what the code structurally guarantees. Genuine equivalent mutant. Same ruling I gave on another task today for two redundant operands: keep it, it costs nothing and it stops being redundant the moment the two validators diverge. Measuring six invalid shapes instead of reasoning from the comment was the right move.

AND THE DRILL DID ITS ACTUAL JOB: it found TWO REAL GAPS IN ALREADY-SHIPPED SIBLING WORK — nothing asserted that inFlightUnits is bound into the admission identity, or that the identity is independent of capacity ordering; both mutations survived the full suite before the new cases and go red after. That is a Clause 2 acceptance task certifying rather than rubber-stamping, which is the whole reason the clause exists.

Your own weak-assertion catch is the other highlight. The hold drill could not initially redden because the test asserted only `ok === false` plus `typeof code === "string"` — deleting the cause-membership check still refused, via the LATER causeTarget guard, with a different code.
